plans.name: Optima Secure+
plans.notes: PIPELINE PROVEN HERE. 3,275 lines. 73 Standard Definitions, Excl01-Excl18, PED 36mo w/ buy-down to 24mo. Product page also fetchable and cross-validates.

verification.correction_2026_09_11: RETRACTING the earlier 'product doesn't exist' finding — it was wrong. Verified directly in a real browser (not WebFetch summarization) at https://www.hdfcergo.com/health-insurance/optima-secure-plus and https://www.hdfcergo.com/download/brochure/health : 'Optima Secure+' is a real, currently-marketed product, and 'Infinite Benefit' (dataset spells it 'Infinity') is real, described on the live product page and in a dedicated 'Optima Secure+ Brochure' (https://customer-portal-assets.hdfcergo.com/documents/OptimaSecure+-BR-Opt2(2)-146549135394.pdf, extracted to extracted/health-hdfcergo-optima-secure-plus-brochure.txt) as: 'Since there is no maximum capping on Infinite Benefit, this cycle of additional 100% every year never stops & continues for infinite times.' This directly matches the dataset's claim.
confirmed: bonus/Infinite Benefit — 100% of base SI added annually, no cap, per the dedicated Optima Secure+ brochure — matches dataset
verification.RESOLVED_2026_09_11: ✅ The prospectus settles it. https://customer-portal-assets.hdfcergo.com/documents/Prospectus_myOptimaSecure-676203564982.pdf (UIN HDFHLIP26058V082526, 15,080 lines, extracted/hdfcergo-optima-secure-prospectus.txt) names 'Optima Secure +' as a plan in its own right and defines the benefit at clause 4.17 — '[Inbuilt in Optima Secure + plan]' — with note (c) stating verbatim: 'There is no maximum limit on accumulation of Infinite benefit.' So the dataset's uncapped claim is correct and is now backed by a regulatory document, not just a brochure. The earlier 'brochure vs wording' contradiction was a false alarm: the policy-wording PDF on the download page covers the other variants and simply does not describe this one. Two dataset corrections fell out of the same document — the benefit's real name is 'Infinite Benefit' (was 'Infinity Benefit' throughout) and entry age has no upper limit (was '18–65 yrs'). Prospectus Section 1: 'The minimum entry age for an adult is 18 years and there is no limit on maximum entry age.'
verification.stillOpen: coverRange floor for this specific variant. The prospectus lists the family ladder (5L/7.5L/10L/15L/20L/25L/50L/75L/1Cr/2Cr) 'depending on the Plan opted' without breaking it down per variant; the Optima Secure+ illustration uses ₹15L. The ₹2 Cr ceiling matches the record. Needs the per-variant SI table or a policy schedule.
verification.recommendation: Do not publish the 'no cap' claim as verified from a wording — it is verified from a brochure only (docType: brochure = weaker, cross-check only). Triangulated across THREE independent official HDFC ERGO documents now (two full policy wordings, UIN HDFHLIP25041V062425 and HDFHLIP26058V082526, plus a Customer Information Sheet, UIN HDFHLIP23123V022223) — all three agree with each other (same 7-variant family, bonus capped at 100%, no 'Infinite Benefit') and all three disagree with two separate brochure printings (both UIN HDFHLIP26058V082526, both describing an uncapped Infinite Benefit). This is a settled, well-corroborated brochure-vs-wording discrepancy, not a missing-document problem — further document searches are unlikely to change the answer. Owner should raise with HDFC ERGO directly if resolution is needed before launch; otherwise publish the bonus field as brochure-sourced with that caveat.
documentsChecked_2026_09_11: extracted/hdfcergo-optima-secure-plus-brochure.txt (brochure, UIN HDFHLIP26058V082526) — describes Infinite Benefit, uncapped
extracted/health-hdfcergo-optima-secure-plus-2.txt (second brochure printing, same UIN) — same claim, corroborates

extracted/hdfcergo-OPTIMA-PLUS-WRONG-PRODUCT.txt (WRONG PRODUCT — 'Optima Plus', UIN HDHHLIP21336V022021, an unrelated older plan: different benefit numbers, no Secure/Plus Benefit/Cumulative Bonus mechanics at all. Kept, and renamed to say so, because its original filename read like a match and cost a detour once already)

extracted/optima_secure_policywordings.txt (Customer Information Sheet, UIN HDFHLIP23123V022223, an older revision of the my:Optima Secure family) — corroborates the wording-side finding, no Infinite Benefit
verification.supersedes: The webSearchAttempted / newerWordingFetched notes below are kept for the record but the 'product doesn't exist' conclusion they supported is wrong.

plans.namingMismatchResolved_2026_09_11: RESOLVED. 'Click 2 Protect Supreme Plus' IS a real, separate HDFC Life product — UIN 101N189V03 — confirmed via https://www.hdfclife.com/term-insurance-plans/click-2-protect-supreme-plus (distinct from 'Click2Protect Super', a different plan). Its brochure lives at https://www.hdfclife.com/content/dam/hdfclifeinsurancecompany/products-page/brochure-pdf/HDFC-Life-click-2-protect-supreme-plus.pdf — this URL 403s to WebFetch directly but works in a real browser (triggers a download); owner downloaded it manually and it's now extracted.

confirmed: Critical illness rider: '60 Critical Illnesses' stated verbatim — exact match to dataset
Suicide exclusion 12 months — matches standard dataset language
Min entry age 18 years

Life Stage Option confirmed — 50% Sum Assured increase on marriage (max ₹50L) or home loan (max ₹50L), 25% on 1st/2nd child birth (max ₹25L), no fresh medicals — matches dataset's 'Life Stage Boost raises your cover at marriage or childbirth'
contradicted: coverRange max: dataset says '₹10 Cr'; the CORRECT product's own wording (not the wrong-product brochure checked earlier) also says 'For all other cases: There is no maximum limit' — this contradiction now confirmed twice, against both the wrong and the right document, and fits the same pattern found on every other term plan (ABSL, ICICI, Bajaj).

CSR: dataset says 99.66%; the product's own brochure states '99.72% Individual Claim Settlement Ratio' (by number of policies, FY 2026). Different figure — though CSR is meant to come from IRDAI's own disclosures per §16.7, not an insurer's self-reported marketing figure, so this may be a different measurement basis (period/method) rather than a straightforward error. Worth resolving against IRDAI data directly rather than either self-reported number.
uncertain: Max entry age: dataset says 65; the wording's eligibility table shows Max. Age at Entry = 85 for the 'Life' and 'Life Plus' plan options, but 65 for 'Life Goal'. Depends which of the three options the dataset record represents — not stated in the dataset.
